title: Bringing a Healthy Options Card Into Use and the Allowance That Comes With It
content:
A card that must be brought into use before it will work carries no spendable allowance until the member brings it into use, and the allowance for the period the programme opened in is made available on that day. This is the standing basis of the Supplemental Benefit Allowance Programmes where a member brings a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card into use.

**What it governs.** The programme is set to in use with that day recorded as the day the card was brought into use, a single load entry on the card's running record carries the allowance made available, placed in the benefit period given, and the spendable balance held on the programme rises by that amount. The card will work at the till from that moment.

**How it is done.** Only the member can do this, because only they can say the card reached them. The representative unlocks the customer tool `activate_allowance_card_a5740baf` and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves, who is the member holding the card.

**Parameters.**

- `allowance_program_id` — Id class: the reference number of the allowance programme being brought into use, which the representative reads out from the member's allowance programme record.
- `card_number_last_four` — Fixed-format class: the last four digits printed on the card the member is holding, exactly four digits with no spaces or punctuation and no other part of the number; an empty value is not accepted.
- `first_load_amount` — Fixed-format class: the allowance made available on the card as it is brought into use, in USD to 2 decimal places, a positive figure; the direction is carried by the entry itself, so no minus sign is used, and an empty value is not accepted.
- `benefit_period` — Fixed-format class: the benefit period the allowance made available belongs to, written as a benefit period as YYYY-Qn, for example 2026-Q2, with the quarter in upper case and no spaces.

**What comes back.** A single line of confirmation text carrying the reference number of the load entry created, the allowance made available in USD to two decimal places, the benefit period it was placed in, the last four digits of the card now in use, and the spendable balance the programme stands at. A line carrying that reference number and the card's last four digits is what indicates the card is in use and the allowance is on it.
